lines.text: Three days later, I was presented at court. Oswin made me practise bowing for an hour. Ash learned faster than I did.
Lucan Varr, Lord of Greyhollow. And... his hound.
The throne room laughed. I had expected that. I had been laughed at by better rooms.
King Edric the Fourth had four rings, a golden crown, and a habit of looking at the Grand Measurer before he said anything at all.
Lord... Lord Lucan. You saved our northern column. Captain Holt speaks very well of you. Very well. We are... grateful.
As is the Order. The Remeasuring will open Your Majesty's Tourney, ten days from now. A great day. Everyone will be there.
Then the King's niece pushed past two dukes to get a better look at me.
So you're the zero. You're shorter than the songs.
There are songs?
Three. Two are about you. The good one is about the dog.
Princess Mirelle. Four rings, Iron, and no patience for anything. Holt told me later she had once broken a suitor's nose in that very hall. He said the suitor deserved it.
Sabine was there too, in purple, with Rafe and Odette. Odette waved at Ash across the whole throne room. Ash wagged, and three courtiers had to dodge his tail.
Lord Lucan. You look much drier.
And then there was the prince.
Prince Aurelio of Calvere, from across the southern sea. A golden circlet, silks the colour of sunrise, and a smile like a warm bath. The whole room was a little in love with him. He knew it.
Lord Lucan! At last. I've bought every rimeglass lamp your counting house in Vask would sell me. Four hundred of them. And I'd like to buy more.
In fact, I'd like to buy everything Greyhollow grows. Whatever it is that makes your people so... remarkable.
Mostly turnips, Highness.
Then I'll take the turnips.
He laughed, and the whole court laughed with him. Only Mirelle didn't. She watched him the way Wren watches a wolf.
As the court broke up, Vance stopped beside me. He smelled of roses, and old paper.
Lord Lucan. Would you take tea with me tomorrow? Just the two of us. I think we should talk, before the whole court does.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter seventy-two, coming soon.
